author: DrSwing
text:
Hi Mike, lots of different techniques here on RTM for entering trades, and you will end up using which ever is comfortable for you. As this is an M5 chart you don't need to dig any deeper, as the zone is very narrow and provides good R:R if you TT the edge. As you can see PA also showed up in the zone, if your preference is to wait on it. My preference here would have been TT trades.

EDIT: I should point out that when we talk about PA here on RTM, we are talking about engulfs of zones, and not individual candle PA, but many here do use candle PA. However I believe IF would say to forget the candles and concentrate on the zones:).

author: DrSwing
text:
I have been asked this question recently. " I find the different methods used confusing and I struggle immensely with them. Is there one thing that I should focus on when trying to learn this stuff? What would be the most important thing that drives all of this?"

I would be surprised if the answer to this would be the same for everyone, so maybe it would be good to get an array of answers from traders you have put it all together. Thanks in advance for your input:).

author: Pedini
text: I'd say the first thing to learn would be the movement of price. Understand the areas price reacts to, and why it is reacting to those areas. Understand who is moving the market and why they move it the way they do. Once you are comfortable understanding WHO and WHY, you can then start learning ways to follow.

author: Red Knight
text:
Hi, As Pedini said'first to understand how price move etc. Stage1 IF made for this video (Not sure name of the video)He explain on instrument -GOLD how price move and why price move(just search in IF video section. 2.Harry in markepedia post where he explain in details FL and FTR concepts 3.Go to Pedini thread and you will find his explain in details PAZ concept+many FL+FTR examples.Start to read from 2013 and sit in his journal and try to understand each his trade. After done all this you will have done build basic fundation for next step which is: Stage2 Go to the IF videos again and find his video about (reading session)then do homework and apply what you had learn already +you will find some new things and put this all together with notes. Stage-3 When you done that go to the classroom I think page 12 and find IF quiz with questions and read all answears specially (Benhur's and Dr.Swing+IF's) after this exercise you will get instructions how to make trading plan for trade before trade and also how you should manage trade after entry. Final stage: After all this you should have your own trading method if not go back to stage-1. When you've done that open again your MT4 and you are ready to practice on demo acc.all what you learn. When you can make money consistently on demo acc. open real acc. but if you can not make consistently money on demo you have two options:

1,Practice harder 2.Forget about trading and try something else.

P.s.It is not about how many hours you will spend learn or about screen time.It is about how you understand all and how you will put all together. So don't count hrs and don't only concentrate watching charts.You need to be active(be teacher and student in the same time).You need to find your own edge in the market.There is not teacher who give you this.Personally I am not using in trading words'easy' 'simple' 'short period of learn'

For me there is not only learn one thing.Understand each concept is easy but harder part is put all together and make on it money. If all this is too much mess here is one tip: Start with every IF post and videos then do the same process with Harry's and Pedini's.Only watching and reading their posts is not enough you need to study deep and understand it(all this is the simple part of you trading journey b/c they explain all in very understandable way even if English is not you mother language).After done all that I am guarantee you will know what you need to do next. First goal is understand concepts. Second goal is consistently making money on your knowledge(Reaching first goal will not automatically guarantee reaching second goal specially in trading bussines).

All the best. RK

author: DrSwing
text:
H, In my view not all demand orders need to get removed in CP, just the larger pockets, to ease the move back down through it. Also you will notice that if you check A1 & A2 areas, marked on the chart below in a LTF, you can see more evidence of demand removal on the way up.

When price returns to the CP zone, these tiny pockets of demand still cause a reaction, but the small numbers of buyers here are easily overcome by the sellers from the flip area of B above. Unless B gets engulfed north the sellers are in control. Once the bottom edge of the PAZ is engulfed south we are free to move into the zone below.

H, the grey areas are just my rough guide to show how the small pockets of demand in the CP on the left caused a reaction on the right, but there was not enough buy orders to push price up through the stronger supply from B above.

Now moving on from that, to my mind there was quite a lot of activity as price was dropping here, and the supply at B has been tapped a couple of times, so maybe there is now actually some accumulation going on here. The spike into the lower zone would have triggered some stops, so the ITs may be looking to take price higher now to a stronger supply area for an eventual move lower.

The ITs need to play games with price so that they can fill their large orders, and it is our job to follow their trail as they move price around, so that we can decipher their intentions.
